scenes.title: Dagster & Software-Defined Assets
scenes.narration: This lesson introduces Dagster and its defining idea, the software-defined asset, which reframes orchestration around data rather than tasks.

scenes.title: Task-centric versus asset-centric

left.heading: Airflow (tasks)
points: The DAG is a sequence of actions

right.heading: Dagster (assets)
points: You define the data you want to exist
The catalog knows what data is fresh

scenes.narration: The core philosophical shift is from tasks to assets. In a task-centric tool like Airflow you declare the actions to run, and the data they produce is only an implicit side effect. In Dagster you instead declare the assets themselves, the tables and datasets you want to exist, and Dagster infers the dependencies between them. This makes the data, not the task, the first-class object the whole system revolves around.

scenes.title: What a software-defined asset is
bullets: A declaration of a persistent data object
A function that computes and materializes it
Dependencies expressed by naming other assets
scenes.narration: A software-defined asset is a declaration of a persistent data object such as a table, paired with the function that computes and materializes it. You express dependencies simply by naming the upstream assets a function needs as its inputs. From these declarations Dagster assembles a complete graph of your data, so it always knows how every asset is produced and what it depends on.

scenes.title: Defining assets in Dagster
scenes.narration: This Dagster code defines two assets. The raw_orders asset fetches data, and the order_summary asset takes raw_orders as a parameter. That parameter name is the dependency: Dagster sees order_summary needs raw_orders and wires the graph automatically. Notice there is no separate DAG definition. The dependencies emerge directly from the function signatures, so the code and the lineage can never disagree.

scenes.title: What this unlocks
bullets: A live asset catalog with freshness and lineage
Re-materialize just the assets that are stale
First-class local testing of each asset function
scenes.narration: Framing everything around assets unlocks powerful capabilities. Dagster maintains a live catalog showing each asset's lineage and freshness, so you can see at a glance what data is stale. You can then re-materialize only the assets that need updating rather than rerunning everything. And because assets are plain functions, each one is straightforward to unit test locally, which is a notable ergonomics win.

scenes.text: Dagster orchestrates the data you want to exist, not just the tasks to run, giving you built-in lineage, freshness, and targeted re-materialization.
scenes.narration: The essential takeaway is that Dagster orchestrates the data you want to exist rather than merely the tasks to run, and that asset-centric model gives you built-in lineage, freshness tracking, and the ability to re-materialize precisely what has gone stale.
